skills.name: Taste — Anti-Slop Frontend
skills.description: Anti-slop frontend skill for landing pages, portfolios and redesigns. Reads the brief, infers the design direction, ships interfaces that never look templated. Note: very long (~87KB).

skills.name: Frontend Design
skills.description: Distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI: aesthetic direction, typography, hero-as-thesis, choices that don't read as template defaults.

skills.name: UI/UX Pro Max
skills.description: AI-powered design intelligence: UI styles, color palettes, font pairings, UX guidelines, chart types across 20+ tech stacks (design-system workflow; on-device data search not bundled).

skills.name: Caveman Mode
skills.description: Ultra-compressed communication. Cuts output tokens ~65% by speaking like a caveman while keeping full technical accuracy. Intensities: lite / full / ultra / wenyan.

skills.name: Superpowers Overview
skills.description: Router skill for the Superpowers family: tells the agent which superpower to reach for (brainstorming, debugging, TDD, plans, reviews).

skills.name: Brainstorming
skills.description: Turn vague ideas into validated designs through structured questioning, alternative exploration and requirement capture before any code is written.

skills.name: Systematic Debugging
skills.description: Four-phase root-cause discipline: reproduce, isolate with binary search, understand the mechanism fully, then fix — no blind patch-and-hope changes.

skills.name: Test-Driven Development
skills.description: Red-green-refactor loop: write the failing test first, watch it fail, write minimal code to pass, refactor with confidence.

skills.name: Writing Plans
skills.description: Write implementation plans that a fresh mind could execute without context: exact files, exact steps, verification per bite-sized task.

skills.name: Executing Plans
skills.description: Work through an implementation plan one task at a time, verifying each step before moving on instead of batching risky work.

skills.name: Requesting Code Review
skills.description: How to hand work to a reviewer so feedback is useful: scope the diff, name the risks, ask specific questions instead of 'looks good?'

skills.name: Receiving Code Review
skills.description: Respond to review feedback like a professional: verify each claim technically, accept what's right, push back with evidence on what isn't.

skills.name: Verification Before Completion
skills.description: Never claim done without running the thing: evidence over confidence — build it, run it, see the output pass before saying success.

skills.name: Subagent-Driven Development
skills.description: Orchestrate narrow-context sub-agents with explicit specs and verification gates between stages for large multi-file work.

skills.name: Ponytail — Lazy Senior Dev
skills.description: Forces the laziest solution that actually works: YAGNI, stdlib before custom code, native features before dependencies, one line before fifty.

skills.name: Ponytail Audit
skills.description: Find what should be deleted in an existing codebase: dead code, speculative abstractions, dependencies doing one line of work.

skills.name: Ponytail Debt Ledger
skills.description: Track shortcuts honestly as debt entries with payback triggers, so deliberate laziness never turns into a trap.

skills.name: Ponytail Gain Review
skills.description: Before building anything, force the question: does the benefit justify the code? Sometimes the answer is don't build it.

skills.name: Ponytail Review
skills.description: Review diffs for over-engineering: needless abstraction, premature flexibility, configuration nobody asked for.

skills.name: Import Memory from Another Assistant
skills.description: Bring memories over from ChatGPT/Gemini/etc.: paste their export, get it filtered (privacy-safe), confirmed, and filed into structured memory/ files additively.
